subject: System Design
title: Cascading Failures
description: A quick, practical guide to Cascading Failures.

hook.text: One server crashes. Traffic shifts to the remaining servers. They become overloaded and crash too. A domino effect.

buildup.text: Cascading failures occur when one failure increases load on other components, causing them to fail as well.

discovery.text: The 2017 S3 outage cascaded because restarting subsystems took hours due to the sheer scale of metadata.

twist.text: Adding retries without backoff accelerates cascading failures. Every retry adds load to an already overwhelmed system.

climax.text: Circuit breakers, load shedding, and exponential backoff are the primary defenses against cascading failures.

punchline.text: One failure triggers many — break the chain early.

quiz.question: What accelerates cascading failures?
options: Retries without backoff adding load to overwhelmed systems
